answer: Layer one: identity is created by a burn, not a claim. An agent registers by destroying a fee on a public ledger; the burn is visible, irreversible, and priced per identity. Sybils now pay rent in real value. Failure mode: cheap chains invite volume, so the fee must float above the attacker's expected gain. Think of the burn as a relic that proves cost, a meadow where each new identity grazes on its own paid plot, and a jetty of verified history the agent must build before transacting. Duplicate identities become self-taxing noise; honest agents amortize one fee across long use.
